To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a single register bank with a small number of multi-ported registers is a good design for embedded processors, (2) a single register file can be made large enough to handle software pipelining without increasing the number of ports, and (3) a single register is a good design, but a single, multiported register file is a good design only if the number of ports is small enough that a single register file is large enough to handle a software-pipelined program.
we have developed a set of techniques for transforming programs to reduce the register pressure of a software-pipelined loop.

The proposed register partitioning scheme, in which the register file is divided into two or more subfiles, can significantly reduce the area and power consumption of the register file, while the register allocation algorithm can reduce the register spill rate by 30% to 60%, compared with the conventional register allocation algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of mapping loop nests onto architectures with partitioned register files, and the associated transformations that can be performed in order to achieve a good mapping.

the problem of how to efficiently map software-pipelined loops to processors with partitioned register files, i.e., processors with multiple register banks that are connected by a register renaming network.
the problem of how to exploit ILP on embedded systems that are constrained in terms of power, area, and cost, but which have the ability to partition the register file into multiple banks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loop transformation techniques presented in this dissertation are useful in reducing the register pressure and improving the performance of embedded applications.
the proposed method can be used as a tool in the design of embedded systems.
the proposed loop transformation techniques can be used to reduce the register requirements of an application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for the automatic transformation of loop nests for architectures with partitioned register banks.
we have designed and implemented a new compiler algorithm for the automatic generation of software pipelined code for architectures with partitioned register banks.
we have developed a methodology to automatically transform programs for architectures with partitioned register banks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the class of architectures with partitioned register banks that we study, it is important to understand and take advantage of the interplay between the loop transformation space, the architecture, and the compiler.
it is possible to use loop transformations to improve performance on architectures with partitioned register banks.
it is possible to build a high performance embedded processor with a partitioned register file, but that it is necessary to use software pipelining to expose the parallelism in the code.
